findings.what: The new public dispatcher rejects only a symlinked `.anomaly`; it still follows case-controlled symlinks for `case.json`, `data/sources.json`, and receipt files. In particular `_registered_sources` reads `data/sources.json` through `_read_case_json`, P1 returns that external JSON, and `WorkflowRunner._write_output` persists it in the case attempt directory.
findings.why: A shared or malicious case can make the installed workflow read host files outside the case and copy valid list-shaped JSON into durable attempt evidence. The existing whole-tree no-symlink validator is called only by `fork_case`, so the public dispatcher has a reachable confidentiality and containment escape before the narrower module guards run.

findings.what: Dataset-derived detector text reaches `findings/report.md` as active Markdown. `detect.py:669` embeds the query-derived `candidate_id` in `statement`; review redaction removes credential patterns but does not escape Markdown/HTML or line breaks before inserting the statement verbatim.
findings.why: A malicious CSV value can produce headings, links, raw HTML, or a remote-image tracking URL in an accepted portable report. Hash-bound review and Gate B preserve provenance but do not make the rendered content inert; opening the generated report can alter its apparent editorial structure or trigger renderer-dependent network content.

evidence.output: Six final changed Python files scanned; no dropped targets; 3 high machine findings; recommendation REVIEW; 12 scanner categories with 2 scanner-only coverage gaps; no dependency-audit failure.

The dynamic-evaluation hit is `ast.literal_eval`, which accepts literals only and is used by the restricted fallback parser for fixed built-in metadata. Both SQL interpolation hits receive positive non-boolean integers from `_validate_limits`, so neither can inject SQL syntax. All three machine hits are refuted.

The dispatcher checks only `.anomaly`. `resume_case`, `_read_case_json`, and receipt enumeration follow other case symlinks; registered-source JSON is returned by P1 and serialized to `result.json`, establishing a concrete external-read and persistence path.

Built-in SQL derives candidate IDs from case data, detector execution copies them into signal statements, and accepted statements are written verbatim as Markdown after secret redaction only. Independent review and Gate B bind the bytes but do not escape the rendering sink.
